title: Partition Array Into Two Arrays to Minimize Sum Difference Problem

content.problemStatement:
You receive an integer array `nums` of `2 * n` integers. You need to partition `nums` into **two** arrays of length `n` to **minimize the absolute difference** of the **sums** of the arrays. To partition `nums`, put each element of `nums` into **one** of the two arrays.

Output *the **smallest** possible absolute difference*.

**Example 1:**

![example-1](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/10/02/ex1.png)

```
Input: nums = [3,9,7,3]
Output: 2
Explanation: One optimal partition is: [3,9] and [7,3].
The absolute difference between the sums of the arrays is abs((3 + 9) - (7 + 3)) = 2.
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input: nums = [-36,36]
Output: 72
Explanation: One optimal partition is: [-36] and [36].
The absolute difference between the sums of the arrays is abs((-36) - (36)) = 72.
```

**Example 3:**

![example-3](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/10/02/ex3.png)

```
Input: nums = [2,-1,0,4,-2,-9]
Output: 0
Explanation: One optimal partition is: [2,4,-9] and [-1,0,-2].
The absolute difference between the sums of the arrays is abs((2 + 4 + -9) - (-1 + 0 + -2)) = 0.
```

**Constraints:**

* `1 <= n <= 15`
* `nums.length == 2 * n`
* `-10^7 <= nums[i] <= 10^7`

notes: The exact-cardinality condition is essential: both selected subsets together must contain exactly n elements.
Use 64-bit arithmetic for subset sums in languages where int may overflow; the final answer is at most 3 * 10^8 under the stated constraints.
solution.approach: Use meet-in-the-middle. Split nums into two halves of size n. Enumerate every subset sum in each half and group sums by the number of selected elements. For every left subset containing k elements, pair it with a right subset containing n-k elements. Sort the right sums for each cardinality and binary-search for the value closest to half of the total sum. The minimum value of |total - 2 * selectedSum| is the answer.

better.description: Split nums into two halves. Enumerate subset sums in both halves and group them by subset size. This reduces the search space from all 2^(2n) subsets to two collections of 2^n subset sums. For each left subset size, combine it with the complementary right subset size using binary search.

optimal.description: The production approach is meet-in-the-middle with cardinality grouping. For every possible number k of chosen elements from the left half, sort all right-half sums containing n-k elements. For each left sum, binary-search the closest right sum to total/2 - leftSum and update the answer from the nearest candidates. This preserves the exact n-element requirement while avoiding enumeration of all 2^(2n) full-array subsets.

bruteForce.complexity: O(n * 2^(2n)) time and O(1) extra space apart from the input.
bruteForce.description: Enumerate every subset of nums, keep only subsets containing exactly n elements, compute its sum, and minimize |total - 2 * subsetSum|. This is conceptually simple but examines O(2^(2n)) subsets, which becomes impractical at n = 15.

solution.timeComplexity: O(n * 2^n) time in the worst case, including subset-sum enumeration and sorting the grouped sums.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(2^n) auxiliary space for the grouped subset sums.

followUps: How would the approach change if the two groups did not need to have equal size?
Why is meet-in-the-middle practical for n <= 15 but not for much larger n?
Can the same idea be implemented with a different data structure instead of binary search?
learningObjectives: Apply meet-in-the-middle to reduce an exponential search over 2n elements.
Use subset cardinality to enforce equal-sized partitions.
Combine subset-sum enumeration with sorting and binary search.
Handle negative values and large integer sums safely.
